articles.title: An insightful breakdown of the CoreWeave situation.
articles.summary:
This one is for the real finance sickos — what the increased cost of capital for CoreWeave means. Marc Rubenstein, a former hedgie, is fairly granular about CoreWeave’s loans, which is helpful for trying to understand this situation. I came away wondering if Nvidia, which I think is is functionally the central bank for the neoclouds, will decide to bail CoreWeave out, and if so, what that will look like.

articles.title: I’m beginning to think the next Xbox will be sold like a cell phone.
articles.summary:
Late yesterday, I laid out five ways Microsoft can try to make lemonade out of RAMageddon, but one feels likelier to me now readers have weighed in: the cell phone subsidy model. In the K-shaped economy, wealthier buyers could buy an “unlocked” Xbox, but most could get it “free” with 36-month (or longer!) subscription.
But I also think many will reject that and stick with what they already have.
[Link: The next-gen Xbox won’t cost you $1,800. It can’t. Can it? | https://www.theverge.com/games/1016134/xbox-helix-price-1800-isnt-affordable-editorial | The Verge]
